intended_object: The spatial dilation x ↦ a·x on ℝ³, written as a linear map. The docstring says it is a helper "used to compute the volumes of scaled balls" in the Campanato–Hölder file.
explanation: The body is `a • LinearMap.id`, which is the homothety x ↦ a x on Vec3, and it is stated correctly. It is not a new notion, though. Mathlib already has it as the expression `a • LinearMap.id` (the same scalar multiple of the identity, available in any module); the counterpart field names its main constant, `LinearMap.id`. The definition only gives that map a name, so the library can apply facts like `Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap` when computing volumes of scaled balls. The docstring says outright that it is an auxiliary device for a computation, not a mathematical concept the library is formalizing. If it were judged as a mathematical object, it would count as faithful.
